EM1015 - Ciencia y Tecnología de Materiales
EM1019 - Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales
EM1020 - Teoría de Máquinas y Mecanismos
EM1028 - Máquinas y Instalaciones de Fluidos

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to justify and evaluate different process plans during integrated teamwork.
Be able to apply ISO language to program CNC machines at a basic level.
Correctly use basic technical manufacturing terminology in English.
Be able to design machining, inspection and/or assembly process plans.
Be able to explain a process plan based on the indications included in the plans.
Be able to relate integral process planning activities with product design and development actions and manufacturing processes.
Be able to build a representative model of the manufacturing process based on process modeling techniques.

syllabus_topics: Interpretation of product geometric data and information.
Geometric analysis and sequence of machining operations.
Selection of cutting tools and machine tools.
Geometric validation: Tolerance planning and control.
teaching_methods: Lectures: exposing theoretical foundations, supported by multimedia presentations, bibliographic material, and whiteboard.
Exercise and problem solving: resolving simple examples by the professor and short problems by students in class, followed by discussion of results.
Laboratory work: practical sessions, some in a computer lab, where students autonomously develop CNC programs using software like CNCSimulator / WinUnisoft.

Project-based learning: group work on process planning for a part, including defining processes, 3D printing models, creating sand molds, molding and cleaning parts, machining process planning, CNC programming, machining in the workshop, and dimensional inspection.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (Process Planning Project - group work, three progress seminars, class presentation, document submission)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must achieve at least 5 out of 10 points in the overall average grade. For the overall average grade to be calculated, students must obtain a minimum of 4 out of 10 in both continuous assessment (project) and the final exam; otherwise, the global average cannot exceed 4 out of 10. In the second call, assessment methods and minimums are the same, with the possibility of recovering the continuous assessment project by submitting and presenting the work before the exam. For the extraordinary call at the end of studies, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade, with no minimum mark required.
